# noctua-colors-tokens

Generated colour tokens from [noctua-colors](https://github.com/noctua-world/noctua-colors). Every colour is
a `const`, so nothing here allocates or costs anything at runtime. The crate
is `no_std` and has **no dependencies** — a consumer of tokens should not
inherit a colour-math library.

This crate is generated output. The colours are not authored anywhere in it:
they are solved from a declarative specification, against APCA contrast
targets, and regenerated on demand. To change a colour, change the spec in
the repository.

## Install

There are 39 palettes, one Cargo feature each, and **only the default
is compiled in**. Ask for the ones you ship:

```toml
# The table form, because an inline table cannot span lines in TOML.
[dependencies.noctua-colors-tokens]
version = "0.2.0"
default-features = false
features = ["ochre_balanced", "blue_vivid"]
```

A feature per palette is not about compile time — the whole crate builds in
about half a second. It is about `.rmeta`: every consumer that names this
crate loads the metadata for whatever is compiled in, which is megabytes at
39 palettes. Use `all` only for a tool that genuinely needs every
palette, such as a picker.

## Use

```rust
use noctua_colors_tokens::{gray, ochre_balanced};

// Every one of these is resolved at compile time.
let surface = ochre_balanced::light::neutral::BG_APP.hex;  // "#fdfdfd"
let accent = ochre_balanced::dark::accent::SOLID;
let packed = accent.packed();                    // 0x00rrggbb
let oklch = (accent.l, accent.c, accent.h);      // as the colour was defined
let step = gray::STEP_18;                        // the shared neutral ramp
```

Module path is `<palette>::<light|dark>::<family>::<ROLE>`. Roles are the
twelve functional steps — `BG_APP`, `BG_SUBTLE`, `BG_ELEMENT`,
`BORDER_SUBTLE`, `SOLID`, `TEXT_STRONG`, and so on — plus numbered steps and
an alpha ladder. The `gray`, `gray_cool` and `gray_warm` ramps are shared by
every palette and are always present.

## Other formats

The same palette is emitted as CSS custom properties, a Tailwind v4 theme,
DTCG tokens, SCSS, JSON/TypeScript and a QML singleton. If you are styling a
web view rather than painting in Rust, the CSS is almost certainly what you
want — see the [repository](https://github.com/noctua-world/noctua-colors) for every installation route.
